column1: # gemini-quota-caps.tsv — per-key, per-model Gemini quota caps (#2030).
# Consumed by scripts/lib/gemini-quota.sh (gq_* helpers), which engine.sh uses for the
# `gemini` branch of check_provider_headroom and for cooldown-aware key rotation, and by
# scripts/token_report.sh for the per-key "Gemini quota" section. Limits are DATA, not
# code: every change is a reviewed PR, and no script hard-codes a Gemini limit.
# SELF-IMPOSED CAPS (#2146). The rows below are NOT the limits Google enforces on these
# keys. They are caps the fleet imposes on itself, set equal to Google's Free Tier limits,
# and they are the same for all four key indexes:
#   gemini-3.8-flash         5 requests/minute, 250000 tokens/minute, 20 requests/day
#   gemini-3.1-pro-preview   0 on every window: Pro is excluded. A $1 balance buys only
#                            about 18 Pro calls.
# Why: each key holds $1 of prepaid credit, paid once (as of 2026-10-09), so its tier is
# `paid`. Google's real Tier 1 limits for a paid key are far higher. Metering against
# those would make every key look healthy until the money is gone.
# These numbers are a maintainer decision. Change them only by a reviewed PR. They are
# never measured by calling the Gemini API and never guessed.
# A row edited back to `unknown` is treated as CONSTRAINED again (headroom result 2,
# rotated after keys with measured headroom): nothing is trusted until it is filled.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   1 key_index   1 = primary slot (GEMINI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY), N = GOOGLE_API_KEY_N.
#                 Keys are identified by index only — never put a key value here.
#   2 model_glob  shell glob matched against the ledger record's model ('*' wildcard).
#   3 tier        free | paid | unknown (informational; shown in the report).
#   4 rpm         requests per minute
#   5 tpm         tokens per minute (metered as input + cache-read + output — over-counts,
#                 which is the conservative direction)
#   6 rpd         requests per day (window: since the last daily reset below)
# Each limit is a non-negative integer, `none` (no cap on that window), or `unknown`.
# A row with ANY `unknown` limit is unknown as a whole.
# Settings rows (`setting<TAB>name<TAB>value`):
#   daily_reset_time      HH:MM the requests/day quota resets; `unknown` → rolling 24h
#                         (counts at least as many calls as any real reset window).
#   daily_reset_tz        IANA timezone of daily_reset_time (e.g. America/Los_Angeles).
#   default_cooldown_sec  how long a key rests after a rate-limit/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED when
#                         the error carries no retry hint. 60 = one requests/minute window.
#                         It doubles per consecutive rejection of the same key and model,
#                         capped at the next daily reset (#2041).
#   history_days          previous days the per-day history (gemini_tier_report.sh) shows
#                         and retains, besides today. GEMINI_HISTORY_DAYS overrides it.
# A cap of 0 makes that key `unavailable` for the model: rotation never calls it there
# (#2041). A key whose requests today reach rpd is `exhausted` until the reset and is
# not called either; keys with `unknown` limits are still tried.
